history.action: route debug -> implement -> review -> qa (label:bug, confidence 90)

validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: The failure was reproduced twice — once in the browser at $PREVIEW_URL following the reporter's exact steps, and once in the repo's own vitest harness through the same AQL path — and the throwing line was then read directly. What is not verified is the fix itself (that is the implementer's job), and whether the reporter's Firefox build differs; the crash reproduced in Chromium, and the throwing code is platform-independent JS so Firefox is not expected to behave differently.
validated_work_order.understanding: Typing a backslash into the value of a `notes matches` rule condition in the rule editor crashes the app with the generic 'Something internally went wrong' banner. The trigger is not the final value the reporter typed (`#\d+` is a valid regex and queries fine) but the intermediate keystrokes on the way there. As each character is typed, RuleEditor re-runs its live preview: `send('make-filters-from-conditions')` turns the condition into `{ notes: { $transform: '$lower', $regexp: value } }`, and `aqlQuery` compiles that to the SQL literal `REGEXP('<value>', UNICODE_LOWER(notes))`. After typing `#` then `\`, the intermediate value `#\` is an incomplete regex, and the SQLite user function `regexp` does an unguarded `new RegExp(regex)`, which throws a SyntaxError. The throw happens inside the SQL engine rather than in application code, so it escapes every caller: it rejects the `aqlQuery` promise inside RuleEditor's `run()`, which is called as `void run()` with no `.catch()`, producing an unhandled rejection; the backend separately emits a `server-error` event, and `handleGlobalEvents` turns that into the red notification banner. Three reported inputs (`#\d+`, `\`, `asdfasdf\`) each crash on the way to being typed; `normal` does not.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The SQLite `REGEXP` user function calls `new RegExp(regex)` with no try/catch, so any syntactically incomplete or invalid pattern the user happens to have typed mid-edit throws a SyntaxError from inside the SQL engine. Because the AQL compiler inlines the user-supplied pattern as a SQL string literal and the throw bypasses application error handling, it rejects the caller's promise (unhandled in RuleEditor's `void run()`) and separately triggers the global `server-error` banner. A partial regex is a normal transient state while typing, not an exceptional one, so the data layer must treat an unparseable pattern as 'matches nothing' — which is exactly what the two sibling regex consumers already do (`Condition.eval`'s `matches` case wraps `new RegExp` in try/catch, and `forecast-filters.ts`'s `$regexp` case does too). The sqlite `regexp` function is the one consumer that was missed.
validated_work_order.approach: Wrap the `new RegExp` call in the sqlite `REGEXP` user function in a try/catch that returns 0 (no match) and logs, matching the existing precedent in `Condition.eval` (`packages/loot-core/src/server/rules/condition.ts:422-427`) and `evaluateClause` (`packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/forecast-filters.ts:255-258`). This is the correct fix location rather than a guard in RuleEditor: `regexp` is the single shared chokepoint every `$regexp` query reaches, so one guard there fixes the rule-editor preview, custom report filters, schedule filtering, and any other AQL caller at once — whereas patching RuleEditor would leave every sibling caller still crashing. Apply the identical change to both platform registrations (`platform/server/sqlite/index.ts` for the browser/sql.js build and `index.electron.ts` for better-sqlite3), since they define the function separately and the reporter's Docker and desktop builds differ. Do not change AQL compilation or the rule editor: an invalid pattern should still compile and simply match nothing, exactly as it already does on the `Condition.eval` path, so a saved rule with an in-progress regex stays inert rather than breaking.

files.change: Wrap `new RegExp(regex)` in the `regexp` function (line ~211) in a try/catch that returns 0 and logs the invalid pattern, so an unparseable regex from a half-typed rule condition returns no rows instead of throwing a SyntaxError out of the SQL engine. Register as before via `db.create_function('REGEXP', regexp)`.
files.why: The throwing line, and the single chokepoint all `$regexp` AQL queries pass through in the browser/sql.js build.

files.change: Apply the same try/catch guard to the separate `regexp` definition (line ~124) registered with `db.function('REGEXP', { deterministic: true }, regexp)`, so the Electron/desktop build behaves identically to the browser build.
files.why: The two platform files define `regexp` independently; fixing only one leaves the desktop build crashing on the same input.

cases: a `notes matches` condition whose value is an incomplete regex (a lone trailing backslash) resolves the query instead of rejecting it, when at least one transaction exists

a `notes matches` condition with a partial pattern reached mid-typing (`#` followed by a backslash) resolves the query instead of rejecting — this is the exact keystroke sequence that crashed the editor
a `notes matches` condition with another unterminated construct (`#[` and `(`) resolves the query instead of rejecting
a valid `notes matches` pattern (`#\d+`) still returns only the transactions it should, so the guard did not turn every pattern into a no-op
a valid regex that matches nothing still returns an empty result rather than throwing
a raw `SELECT ... WHERE REGEXP('<invalid pattern>', string)` through runQuery returns no rows instead of throwing, pinning the guard at the sqlite function itself
a raw `SELECT ... WHERE REGEXP('n.', string)` still matches as before, so existing regexp behaviour is unchanged

acceptance.how_to_verify: Rules > New rule > condition field `notes`, op `matches`. Type `#`, then `\`, then `d`, then `+` one character at a time. No 'Something internally went wrong' notification appears at any point, the condition editor remains rendered, and the browser console records no unhandled rejection.

acceptance.check: The final complete value `#\d+` still functions as a regex: after finishing the input, the preview shows the transactions whose notes match, exactly as before the change.

acceptance.how_to_verify: Save the rule with an invalid pattern, then open a transaction and confirm the rule list loads and the transaction view renders normally with no error notification.

acceptance.check: A regression test asserts that a `notes matches` condition with an incomplete regex resolves the AQL query rather than rejecting it, with a transaction present in the database so the REGEXP function is actually invoked per row.

qa_script: Open the app, choose 'View demo' from the initial setup screen (Don't use a server), and let the demo budget finish loading.
Navigate to Rules (More > Rules if the link is collapsed).
In the first condition row set the field to `notes` and the operator to `matches`.
Click the value input and type `#`, then a single backslash, then `d`, then `+` — one keystroke at a time, pausing ~1s between characters so each intermediate value is previewed.
Assert no red 'Something internally went wrong' notification appears at any point and the condition editor is still rendered and interactive.
Confirm the final value `#\d+` shows the demo transaction whose notes contain `#123` in the 'This rule applies to these transactions' table.
Clear the input and type just a single backslash; assert again that no error banner appears and the preview table is simply empty.
Save the rule, then open an account and confirm the transaction list renders with no error notification.
evidence: Browser, $PREVIEW_URL (chromium, demo budget): followed the reporter's steps — Rules > New rule, condition field `notes`, op `matches`. Typing `#\d+`, `\`, and `asdfasdf\` each raised the red 'Something internally went wrong. You may want to restart the app...' banner (that string is defined in packages/desktop-client/src/notifications/notificationsSlice.ts:70). Typing `normal` produced no banner, confirming the trigger is the backslash and not the field/op selection.

The banner was preceded by an unhandled page rejection (`PAGEERROR: Object`) and by the backend logging the failing SQL: `WHERE ((REGEXP('#\', UNICODE_LOWER(v_transactions_internal_alive.notes))))` — note the pattern is the intermediate `#\`, not the final `#\d+`, which is what identifies the mechanism as a per-keystroke throw rather than a bad final value.
Backend console showed the throw surfacing through the query stack: `[Exception] Error at c.handleError ... at runQuery$1 ... at execQuery$1 ... at execTransactionsBasic`.

Isolated the mechanism in the sqlite `REGEXP` function itself: calling `new RegExp(pattern).test(text)` with the compiled literal reproduces the exact message. Patterns `\`, `asdfasdf\`, `a\`, `#[` and `(` all throw `SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression ...`; `#\d+`, `hello`, `#` and `\\` succeed.

Reproduced a second time inside the repo's own vitest harness through the real AQL path (`conditionsToAQL` -> `aqlQuery` on `q('transactions')`), which printed: `"#\\d+" => OK [{"id":"1"}] || "\\" => THREW Invalid regular expression: /\/: \ at end of pattern || "asdfasdf\\" => THREW Invalid regular expression: /asdfasdf\/: \ at end of pattern || "#[" => THREW Invalid regular expression: /#[/: Unterminated character class`. This matches the browser exactly.

Important harness detail found while reproducing: with an empty transactions table the query does NOT throw, because SQLite only invokes a per-row user function when at least one row is scanned. A regression test must seed at least one transaction or it will pass on the broken code — this is why a first attempt at the test passed against the unfixed code.

Confirmed the two sibling regex consumers already guard and return no-match: `Condition.eval` wraps `new RegExp` in try/catch at packages/loot-core/src/server/rules/condition.ts:422-427, and `evaluateClause` does the same for `$regexp` at packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/forecast-filters.ts:255-258. Existing test `matches handles invalid regex` (packages/loot-core/src/server/rules/index.test.ts:231-234) covers only the `Condition.eval` path.

Confirmed the crash surface, not just the crash: the rejected `aqlQuery` promise in RuleEditor is called as `void run()` with no `.catch()` (packages/desktop-client/src/components/rules/RuleEditor.tsx:1085-1104), so it becomes an unhandled rejection; independently the backend emits `server-error` (packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/connection/index.ts:81) and `handleGlobalEvents` (packages/desktop-client/src/global-events.ts:23-25) dispatches `addGenericErrorNotification`, producing the banner.

Confirmed `regexp` is defined twice, independently, and both need the same change: packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.ts:211 (browser/sql.js) and packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.ts:124 (better-sqlite3).

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a try/catch around the `aqlQuery` call in RuleEditor's preview effect, so a bad pattern just yields an empty preview list.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Fixes the symptom at one call site and leaves the crash live for every other `$regexp` consumer — custom report filters, schedule filtering, and any other AQL query built from a user-supplied regex would still throw out of the SQL engine and hit the same global error banner. The debugger guidance is explicit that one guard in the shared function is both the smaller diff and the correct fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Validate the regex in `Condition`'s parse step (or in `conditionsToAQL`) and reject the condition with a 'Invalid regex' field error, mirroring the existing `assert` error types.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Plausible as a UX improvement — showing a field error is friendlier than a silently empty preview — but it changes user-visible behaviour well beyond the reported bug (a previously accepted rule with an invalid pattern would start erroring), and it does not protect the other `$regexp` callers. Worth a follow-up ticket, not this fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Escape or otherwise normalise the pattern in the AQL compiler's `$regexp` case before inlining it as a SQL string literal.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Addresses a real adjacent weakness (the compiler only escapes single quotes, not the value's meaning) but it is not the cause here. The value reaching SQLite is correct — `#\d+` is the user's intended regex — and the throw happens in the JS engine, after the SQL string is well-formed. Escaping would change matching semantics for every valid regex, which is a much larger and riskier change.

alternatives_considered.approach: Escape the backslash before compiling so `#\` is treated as a literal backslash rather than an incomplete escape.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Wrong semantics. `matches` is a documented regex operator; users type `\d`, `\s`, `\\` deliberately. Escaping would break every working regex to fix the crash.

alternatives_considered.approach: Debounce the live preview so intermediate keystrokes are never queried.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Would reduce how often the crash fires but not remove it — paste, autofill, and any single invalid keystroke still throws. It hides the throw rather than fixing the cause.

risks: Returning 0 for an invalid pattern means such a query silently matches nothing. That matches the behaviour already established for `Condition.eval` and `forecast-filters`, so a rule saved with a broken pattern is inert rather than destructive — but it does mean a typo in a regex is quiet. A follow-up UX ticket for a visible 'invalid regex' field error would address that.

The fix touches a shared SQLite function used by every `$regexp` query. The guard is additive and only changes behaviour on the previously-throwing path, so valid patterns are unaffected — but `yarn test` should be run in full to confirm no test depended on the throw.

`regexp` is registered separately in the sql.js and better-sqlite3 platform files. Missing the Electron one would leave the desktop build crashing on the same input, so both files must change in the same commit.

This addresses the crash only. The unhandled `void run()` rejection in RuleEditor's preview effect remains a latent way for any future query error to surface as a full-app error banner; that is a separate robustness concern, not part of this fix.
out_of_scope: Showing a visible 'Invalid regex' error on the rule condition field instead of a silently empty preview — a UX follow-up, deliberately not bundled with the crash fix.
Adding a `.catch()` to RuleEditor's `void run()` preview effect to stop any query failure from becoming a global error banner. Related but a distinct robustness change with its own trade-offs.
The upstream issue at actualbudget/actual#6317 remains open; this fixes the crash in this copy only.
